questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A Chinese proverb states that ‘One generation plants a tree and the next generation enjoys its shade’. Which economic concept does the proverb best illustrate?

options.A: comparative advantage
options.B: division of labour
options.C: positive externality
options.D: public good

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the marginal social benefit (MSB) and marginal social cost (MSC) from a production process.
MSC $ MSB, 4 MSC MSB 0 10 20 output What is the socially desirable level of output?

options.A: at 0 units because MSC is zero
options.B: between 0 and 10 units because MSB is greater than MSC
options.C: at 10 units because MSB equals MSC
options.D: at 20 units because MSB is exhausted

If a firm is making normal profit, it must be true that

options.A: average cost equals average revenue.
options.B: marginal cost equals average cost.
options.C: marginal cost equals average revenue.
options.D: marginal cost equals marginal revenue.

questions.questionText: For which market structure can a market supply curve be constructed?

options.A: imperfect competition
options.B: monopoly
options.C: oligopoly
options.D: perfect competition

A firm incurs both fixed and variable costs of production. It is currently producing at the level of output which minimises its average total cost. What effect will a small reduction in output have on the firm’s marginal and average variable costs? average marginal cost variable cost

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall
options.D: rise rise

options.A: no no yes
options.B: no yes no
options.C: yes no no
options.D: yes yes yes

questions.questionText: What is true about economies of scale but not diseconomies of scale?

options.A: They occur because average revenue is increasing.
options.B: They occur because of management policy changes.
options.C: They occur in the short run.
options.D: They occur with decreasing average cost.

questions.questionText: In which circumstances are a firm’s objectives most likely to differ from profit maximisation?

options.A: when a firm finances new investment largely by retained profits
options.B: where firms are companies with very active shareholders
options.C: where investment banks make takeovers easy to implement
options.D: where there are a large number of individual shareholders in a firm run by employed managers

questions.questionText: What will happen if a firm is subsidised by an amount equal to the external benefits that it gives to the rest of society?

options.A: Resource allocation will be improved.
options.B: The firm will produce less.
options.C: There will be a misallocation of resources.
options.D: There will be no effect upon production.

questions.questionText: A firm is operating in a perfectly competitive market. Why does the marginal revenue product of a factor of production employed by the firm fall as more of the factor is employed?

options.A: Its average revenue falls.
options.B: Its marginal physical product falls.
options.C: Its marginal revenue falls.
options.D: The supply price of the factor rises.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a firm’s total product of labour (TPL) curve. TPL total product of labour O N N N
What would cause a perfectly competitive firm’s marginal revenue product of labour curve to shift to the right?

options.A: a higher rate of sales tax
options.B: a rise in the price of the final product
options.C: an increase in labour supply
options.D: an increase in wages

questions.questionText: It has been argued that when income tax rates imposed on individuals are increased from zero towards 100%, tax revenue initially increases, but at some point it will decrease. If this argument is correct, it follows that

options.A: governments should forgo any attempt to relieve poverty via fiscal policy.
options.B: income tax rates should be set to maximise government tax revenue.
options.C: taxes should be levied on expenditure rather than income.
options.D: there are limits to the redistributive effects of progressive taxation.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for new cars. Currently the quantity supplied is fixed by the government at S . S S x y price z w D O quantity If the market was deregulated the supply curve would be S . Which area measures the net welfare gain of removing the restriction on the quantity supplied?

options.A: w + y B x + y C z + w D z + x + y + w

questions.questionText: What adjustments to real GNP per head might make it a more reliable indicator when comparing standards of living in different countries?

options.A: adjustments to allow for differences in the level of government spending in different countries
options.B: adjustments to allow for differences in the rates of inflation in different countries
options.C: adjustments to allow for differences in the size of the hidden economy in different countries
options.D: adjustments to allow for differences in the value of exports from different countries

questions.questionText: The table shows real GDP per head measured in $US for countries X and Y over a three year period. country 2011 2012 2013 X 100 110 121 Y 200 210 231 What can definitely be concluded from the data?

options.A: Each country had the same rate of economic growth between 2011 and 2012.
options.B: Growth in real GDP per head was higher in country X than in country Y between 2011 and 2012.
options.C: Population growth was higher in country X than in country Y between 2012 and 2013.
options.D: The average price level was higher in country X than in country Y throughout the period.

questions.questionText: Which combination is usually found in developing countries?

options.A: a low birth rate and a dominant primary sector
options.B: capital-intensive production and a rapidly growing population
options.C: external debt and a low death rate
options.D: labour-intensive production and a low rate of saving

questions.questionText: The table refers to changes in the percentage age distribution in a developing country between 2012 and 2014. There has been no emigration or immigration in this period. % of population in each age group year 0 - 15 years 16 - 64 years 65 years and over 2012 25 60 15 2014 30 58 12 Between 2012 and 2014 what can be deduced?

options.A: The average age of the total population has increased.
options.B: The death rate has increased.
options.C: The infant mortality rate has risen.
options.D: The percentage of the dependent population has increased.

questions.questionText: What is a cause of seasonal unemployment?

options.A: a general decrease in the demand for goods and services
options.B: a lack of necessary skills in the workforce
options.C: a temporary change in the pattern of consumers’ expenditure
options.D: an unwillingness of workers to move to other parts of the country where there is work

questions.questionText: What is a possible combination of a cost and a benefit of rising levels of unemployment? cost benefit

options.A: a deterioration in human capital an increase in capital expenditure
options.B: an increase in import expenditure a decrease in government tax revenue
options.C: an increase in the rate of economic growth a more responsive workforce
options.D: an irretrievable loss of output a reduction in inflationary pressure

questions.questionText: Which is likely to cause a decrease in the public’s desired ratio of cash to bank deposits?

options.A: a decrease in the number of reported street crimes
options.B: an extension of bank opening hours
options.C: the introduction of a charge per transaction on accounts
options.D: the introduction of annual charges for the use of credit cards

questions.questionText: What is the aim of stabilisation policy?

options.A: to keep the exchange rate stable
options.B: to keep the price level stable
options.C: to reduce fluctuations in interest rates
options.D: to reduce fluctuations in national output

questions.questionText: The government of Lesotho introduces a programme to promote exports and to encourage firms to expand by subsidising local entrepreneurs. options.C: to ensure that the composition of output matches the pattern of demand
